cover.headline: 5 lessons from leading backend teams
cover.subhead: What actually moved the needle at Acme Corp

slides.headline: Review culture beats review process
slides.body: The best teams I've led cared more about how feedback was given than what tool enforced it.
slides.visual_note: A simple two-column icon comparison: process vs. culture.

slides.headline: Ownership beats heroics
slides.body: Clear ownership prevented more outages than any amount of on-call heroics ever did.
slides.visual_note: An icon of a shield or a name tag next to a service diagram.

slides.headline: Mentoring flows both ways
slides.body: Junior engineers taught senior ones more often than the org chart would suggest.
slides.visual_note: Two arrows pointing toward each other between two figures.

slides.headline: Distributed systems reward patience
slides.body: The fastest fix is rarely the right one when the system spans multiple services.
slides.visual_note: A slow-motion clock icon next to a system diagram.

slides.headline: Small, frequent feedback beats big reviews
slides.body: Teams that reviewed in small batches shipped with fewer surprises.
slides.visual_note: A bar chart comparing batch sizes.

closing.cta: Which of these matches your own experience? Tell me below.

response.caption: Five things I actually learned leading backend teams at Acme Corp -- not the theory, the practice.
